title: Isometrization of Tensor Network States via Gauge Propagation
abstract: We introduce a gauge-propagation approach for approximately converting generic tensor-network states into an isometric tensor-network state form with a prescribed orthogonality center. In one dimension, this propagation is exact because the non-isometric factor produced by a QR or singular-value decomposition is supported on a single virtual bond. In higher-dimensional networks, however, a local step can have several outgoing directions, and the residual factor is generally not separable into independent single-bond contributions. We address this local obstruction by approximating a local tensor, or a contracted local cluster, by structured terms consisting of an isometric factor multiplied by a tensor product of output-leg factors. The isometric factor is retained at the current site or cluster, while the output-leg factors are absorbed into neighboring tensors along the propagation directions. This construction provides a local truncation criterion for gauge propagation and a practical route to refinement by increasing the number of retained terms or enlarging the local cluster. Benchmarks on random tensors and on the loop-gas tensor representation of the Kitaev spin liquid show that this refinement reduces both local residuals and accumulated propagation errors. For the loop-gas tensor, two structured terms reduce the local residual to numerical precision, and enlarging the local object from 2-in-2-out to 4-in-2-out and 6-in-2-out clusters lowers both local truncation errors and accumulated errors in finite honeycomb gauge propagation. These results identify propagation-compatible local decomposition as a useful building block for approximate isometrization and as a potential initializer or preconditioner for variational isoTNS algorithms.
summary: This work introduces a novel gauge-propagation approach to approximate the conversion of general tensor networks into isometric forms. By developing a structured local decomposition, it provides a systematic way to manage non-isometric residuals in higher dimensions. The method is shown to effectively reduce errors when applied to models like the Kitaev spin liquid, offering a powerful tool for variational optimization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of converting generic tensor-network states into an isometric form (isoTNS) by developing a gauge-propagation approach.
main_result: A structured local decomposition method is proposed that allows for controlled approximation of non-isometric tensors, showing significant error reduction when applied to models like the Kitaev spin liquid.
method: The core technique involves defining a propagation-compatible local decomposition where complex residuals are approximated as sums of structured terms, enabling iterative refinement via truncation.
model_or_system: The method is tested on random tensors and specifically on the loop-gas tensor representation used for describing the Kitaev spin liquid (KSL) on honeycomb lattices. It applies to general tensor network states (e.g., MPS/PEPS).
key_observables: Local residuals, accumulated propagation errors ($\Delta_\ell$), normalized overlap ($O_\ell$), and truncation error bounds ($\epsilon_m$).
important_parameters: The local cluster size (e.g., 2-in-2-out up to 6-in-2-out) and the number of retained structured terms ($m$) are key parameters controlling approximation quality.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the residual factor can be approximated by a sum of absorbable, structured local tensors; in higher dimensions, this requires an approximation due to structural obstructions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate gauge propagation geometry on 1D and 2D lattices. Benchmarks compare decomposition methods for random and LG tensors, showing error reduction upon increasing the number of retained terms or enlarging the local cluster size.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the goal (isoTNS via gauge propagation), contrasts exact 1D propagation with obstructed higher-dimensional cases, develops the structured local decomposition approximation, analyzes its convergence using multi-term truncation bounds, and finally validates it by simulating error accumulation on a finite honeycomb lattice.
why_interesting: The development of robust, systematic methods for enforcing physical constraints (like isometry) within tensor network representations is crucial for accurately simulating strongly correlated quantum materials where standard contractions fail due to gauge redundancy.
